analysis.evidence: וְגַם לְלוֹט means “and Lot too.” The verse adds Lot, who traveled with Abram, as another possessor of flocks, cattle, and tents.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וְ means “and.” The additive particle גַם means “also” and places the focus on לְלוֹט.

analysis.evidence: In הַהֹלֵךְ אֶת אַבְרָם, אֶת means “with” and identifies Abram as Lot’s traveling companion.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes a Qal active participle, masculine singular absolute, describing Lot.

analysis.evidence: הַהֹלֵךְ אֶת אַבְרָם describes Lot as “the one traveling with Abram.” Abram is Lot’s companion and is the explicit complement of אֶת. The source gloss “with you (plural)” would require a pronominal suffix.
analysis.morphology: Simple Hebrew preposition with no prefix or pronominal suffix.

draft.change: Link the existing Abram article to אבה through its father element and add Genesis 12:4 as an example.
draft.definition: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham. The name means “exalted father.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:4 repeats the name אַבְרָם when giving Abram’s age at departure. The name’s אָב element belongs to Haqor’s אבה article.

analysis.evidence: הַהֹלֵךְ אֶת אַבְרָם describes Lot as traveling with Abram. אַבְרָם names Lot’s companion.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal name with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham
